subject: health
title: Correction and reflection: community health action
essentialQuestion: How can understanding safety, decisions, and community health help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: Community health actions address a shared condition through accurate information and a realistic request; effective action identifies who can make the change and how progress will be checked.
A defensible community response uses accurate data, identifies the actor with authority, proposes a feasible change, protects privacy and access, and defines how progress will be measured.
For community health action, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Develop a safety and advocacy plan for a fictional home, school, sport, or online scenario.
studentTask: Draft a one-page fictional community response about community health action: state the condition with two facts, identify who has authority to act, propose one feasible change, name a privacy or access safeguard, and define one measure that would show progress.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in community health action; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the community health action task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required. Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model. Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits. Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options. Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media. Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
extensionChallenge: Apply community health action under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.

trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety or health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of community health action in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.

contentProvenance.objective: Use error evidence to choose a different representation or strategy for community health action, then demonstrate corrected understanding.
